findings.text: Advisory (Q10). `heldByContract`'s doc comment now sits above `CONTRACT_READ_MS`, a constant it does not describe. Round 1's defect is resolved: I checked that `spokenAfterMe` (servers.ts:449) is the one rule, called by run.ts:102 and binding.ts:203.
Advisory (Q1). `bindMessage` tells the person to use CLI flags (`--create`, `share names`), and the viewer shows the same sentence in its toast.
Advisory (Q2). The `names.<state>` flags are cleared in a third place. backup.ts:238 also writes its own `'names.%'` prefix. This carries round-1 F-2.
Advisory (Q2, boilerplate). The bare-404 branch is written three times (lines 225, 316, 376).
Advisory (Q2). The 409 step-down in `pushUnderContract` repeats the inline step-down in inbound.ts `fetchPage`.
Advisory (Q8). The re-export of `NAME_STATES`, `NameState` and `nameFlagKey` is unused in src.
Advisory (Q9). The key type makes this guard unreachable, but it throws loudly, so it hides nothing.
Advisory (Q5). `currentItemsUnder` only forwards to `nameCountsOf`.
Advisory (Q3/Q6). The contract that brought shared names is a bare `2` in several files, with no named constant.
Advisory (Q6). On a create or join at `all`, the imported count prints twice: on the would-leave line and again after the bind.
Advisory (Q2). `levelPhrase` and the create and join questions copy the CLI's text, and `hasField` is repeated inline in the template.
Advisory (Q9). When the client's `id` is already in use, the route quietly makes a new id and still answers 201.
Advisory (Q11). The withdrawal sentence leaves out the held-withdrawal case (D-10).
Advisory (Q10/Q11). The `NameState` doc does not mention that the flags are also cleared on server removal and on a restore.
Advisory (Q10). The comment narrates the change ('as before') instead of saying why.
Advisory, debt. The diff did not write this line ('a 409 on the contract stops it'), so it is outside the change.

Advisory (Q4). No red was recorded on this assertion for AC-48. The test does pin the rule and would fail if the rule were reverted. Round-1's Q3 defect on this case is resolved: AC-48 now names it for AC-47.
Advisory (Q1, partial). The no-request check counts only one URL, so a `/v1/me` read or a POST would go unseen.
Advisory. The test does not tell parallel reads from sequential ones, and the fixture has no stopped row.
Advisory (Q2). 'A remote is never listed' holds by how the fixture is built.
Advisory. The no-SQL check searches for two call shapes only, and the order 'after `purged`' has no test.

Advisory. Edge cases the plan lists are still unwritten: the 101st name, no D-10 hold on a `name` refusal, and `one-server` at the CLI. Round 1's six upheld defects are each resolved, by the reviewer's re-check against the code.
Advisory, debt. The old substring assertion does not pin the `no-name` advice.
Advisory. A member who knows a lost name's id can re-create it. This does not widen what any member could already do.
Advisory. A purged name keeps its alias and creator in `team.db` until the database is rebuilt. ADR 0028 states this limit, and only the operator sees it.

Advisory. The client accepts a contract of 0 or a negative integer from a hostile server. This fails closed: the server stops as `contract`. A floor of 1 would only harden the input. Round-1 F-3 is resolved.
Advisory, debt. Any member may pull any alias (ADR 0026 D-11). The diff does not change this.

Upheld (Q2, undeclared reachable branch), on the diff-line branch: review/ui-evidence.json is absent. The diff adds this branch at lines 338-343. I checked it in the code: when `reason` is `exists` and the body carries `name` after 'Create and share', the dock switches to the join sentence and reopens the confirmation as a join. Spec line 269 names this journey ('the dock shows the join state and asks again'). None of the 19 declared /projects states in review/ui/manifest.json covers it, and a capture cannot show a state nobody declared. Declare it and capture it, at least at the plan's narrowest and widest widths.

Lowered to advisory. The cited consoles (review/ui/console-projects-created@*.json and console-projects-removed@*.json) are not listed in a review/ui-evidence.json, because none exists. The diff-line branch takes only what a capture cannot show, and a console line is exactly what a capture shows. On the substance: spec.md:219 pins 409 for `exists`, `purged` and a refusal after a create, and tests/integration/ui-sharing.test.ts pins those statuses. The line is the browser logging that status, and the manifest's observation records it. The dock shows the refusal as a sentence, so no raw error reaches the user.
Advisory (Q5). The created-name sentence starts lowercase and has no full stop (projects-created@1280-dark.png).
Advisory. 'Set the level again' does not name the path that works (Nothing first, then a level). The wording is the spec's own.
Advisory (Q5). Raw Markdown backticks show around the slug in several sentences, while the bound sentences render the slug as code. The taken sentence has no full stop.
Advisory. In the dark scheme, the disabled field in the held state looks the same as the enabled one (projects-held@1280-dark.png).

Advisory (Q7, crowding that holds). The name lines wrap into three or four lines at 360px (settings-flagged@360-dark.png). Round 1's Servers.vue defect is resolved: the `flagged` state is now declared and captured.
Advisory. In the remote-too state, two 'set Nothing' instructions appear one after the other.
Advisory. The spec says the bound field stays read-only; the build removes it. The result reads clearly.

Advisory. The reserved-file-name refusal and the post-confirm 'Not changed' toast reuse captured templates with strings no capture shows. The templates themselves are captured (projects-refused, projects-not-changed).
Advisory, debt. At 768px the list column collapses with the dock open. This is list code the diff did not touch.
Advisory, debt. The server pill stays a green 'Ok' while names are held. The diff did not touch the pill.
Advisory. A missing name is retried on every sweep with no backoff. It is visible as `missing` in `status`, `doctor` and the dock.
Advisory (Q3). `serve purge name` has no dry run and no undo. It is an operator command behind `--yes`, not a first-run write of the deploy.

Advisory, as filed. After a rollback to 0.7.0, the runbook says members read `missing`, when they read `names held` until the next upgrade. spec.md:296 states the order correctly, and the failure is visible. The rollback exists, so no rollback is missing.
Advisory. The rollback is manual and gives no way to list the names the copy predates.
Advisory. After a restore older than a name, a Receive-only teammate's copies are dropped with nothing on their side to explain it. This needs an operator restore, not a deploy.
Advisory, as filed. The client rollback is stated in the spec and in ADR 0028. What remains is a sentence the release notes owe, and that falls to the release item.
Advisory, debt. A stale `serve.lease` makes the new image restart repeatedly until the lease expires. The runbook now documents it.
Advisory, debt. An older binary refuses the version 8 store and its hooks fail open. Every store bump has carried this risk.

Advisory. `nameId` is typed as required, but a contract-1 server never sends it. Nothing reaches the gap today, because names are held at contract 1. Round 1's defect is resolved: I checked that `RESULT_SHAPES` pins `contractRefusal` and `nameConflict` (lines 109 and 111).
Advisory. The contract that brought names is a bare `2`, and the doc comment at line 430 is separated from the function it describes.
Advisory. `listedName` writes the `name:` prefix by hand although `NAME_PREFIX` is already imported.
Advisory, debt. The fallback to a body `retryAfterSec` reads a field no server sends.
Advisory, debt. Inline project-name lookups have no shared helper.
Advisory (Q2). `importedStayCounts` filters on `origin` with no index, a full pass per preview. The result is correct.
Advisory (Q2). Each listed name costs up to three indexed queries. ADR 0028 records this choice.
Advisory (Q2). `receivedNameCounts` filters on `remote_alias` with no index and reads the same rows twice. Round 1's flag and retention points are resolved, by the reviewer's check against the code.
